ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, as amended; Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism (Definitions) Regulations 2003; Companies Act 1993, including the significant-controller/ultimate-ownership transparency provisions administered by the Registrar of Companies; Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013; New Zealand Sanctions Act 2022 and designated-persons regulations.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarised colour copy of the ultimate beneficial owner's current passport
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport-issuing authority or notary public in the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the issuing state is a party to the Hague Apostille Convention 1961; otherwise consular legalization at the New Zealand Embassy or High Commission

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address of the ultimate beneficial owner (utility bill or bank statement issued within 90 days)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or regulated bank in the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarised copy followed by Hague Apostille; if the issuing state is not a Convention state, consular legalization at a New Zealand diplomatic post

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation, register of directors, and register of shareholders for any corporate entity in the UBO ownership chain above the 25% threshold
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign companies registry or Registrar of Companies in the corporate UBO's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the competent authority of the foreign jurisdiction; otherwise consular legalization at a New Zealand Embassy, High Commission, or Consulate

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all directors, UBOs, signatories, and material agents against the OFAC SDN List, United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, HM Treasury consolidated list where passport or residence jurisdiction so indicates, and New Zealand domestic designated-person and sanction regimes under the New Zealand Sanctions Act 2022. Politically Exposed Persons identified by role, jurisdiction, and family/close-associate relationship trigger enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification, and senior-management approval before engagement. Continuous re-screening at least every 90 days and on any material ownership change is required for AML/CFT reporting entities under the AML/CFT Act 2009.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office Name Reservation and Company Search portal (companiesoffice.govt.nz), together with the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) register
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names may be registered in English or te reo Māori using Latin-script characters. Where a name is in a non-Latin script, a Latin-script transliteration must be supplied and the name must be searchable in the Companies Register. Names of limited-liability companies must carry the statutory designator 'Limited', 'Ltd', or 'Tapui Limited'. The Companies Office assesses phonetic identity and near-identity against existing and reserved names under the Companies Act 1993 and Companies (Registration) Regulations 1994.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within the 20-working-day reservation window, the applicant may submit additional evidence, regulator consent letters, or no-objection certificates requested by the Registrar. If the proposed name is rejected, the applicant may file a written reconsideration request with the Registrar of Companies, attaching the relevant ministerial or regulator approvals for each prohibited token. A further refusal may be challenged by judicial review or statutory review in the High Court of New Zealand under Part 30 of the High Court Rules from the date of the Registrar's final determination; the applicant may also submit a fresh name reservation application for the same or a revised name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for an ISIC 5820 digital esports platform. The registered office must be a physical address in New Zealand and may not be a P.O. Box. A virtual-office arrangement may satisfy the Companies Act 1993 requirement if a licensed corporate-services provider maintains a physical New Zealand registered office, accepts legal process, and is available during normal business hours. No local staff are required at pre-incorporation for this remote, low-risk digital service.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (quantified annual risk below 5%). A purely online esports matching and tournament platform with no physical premises, no cash handling, and a low AML/CFT risk tier has minimal expected unannounced inspections; however, the Registrar of Companies and AML/CFT supervisors retain the right to inspect registered-office premises and records with prior notice or under warrant in suspicious circumstances.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), ss 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 18, 19, 38, 87, 88, 122, 124, 128, 153, 158, 165, 189, 193, 211, 234; Companies (Incorporation) Regulations 2006, regs 4-9; Companies (Directors' Addresses) Regulations 2014; Financial Reporting Act 2013 (ss 17-22); Income Tax Act 2007 (s HR 13 for non-resident or international company tax status); Tax Administration Act 1994 (ss 24B-24D, 59, 62) for IRD registration and foreign trust / international company disclosure.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (NZCO), a business unit of the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), operating the New Zealand Companies Register and online portal at companiesoffice.govt.nz.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form R – Application for Incorporation of a Company (prescribed form under Companies (Incorporation) Regulations 2006, Schedule 1), submitted electronically through the Companies Office 'Company Online' service.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up or issued share capital is required for a New Zealand limited liability company under s 38 of the Companies Act 1993. The company may be incorporated with nominal or even zero capital; no escrow account is mandated by the Companies Office. Share capital may be expressed in any currency. If the entity elects an 'International Company' tax classification, no additional capital contribution is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FIRST WRITTEN RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED (the 'Company'), passed pursuant to sections 122 and 124 of the Companies Act 1993 on [___] 20[___]. The following resolutions are duly passed unanimously by all directors and shareholders of the Company:

1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: RESOLVED that the initial share capital of the Company shall be subscribed and allotted as follows: [Shareholder Name] (resident at [address]) subscribes for [number] ordinary shares at par / at a premium of NZD [amount] per share, fully paid or credited as fully paid. The total consideration of NZD [amount] has been received by the Company and shall be held as working capital. No statutory escrow account is required in light of the absence of a minimum capital requirement under the Companies Act 1993.

2. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company in New Zealand is fixed at [full physical address, street, city, New Zealand], and the Registrar of Companies is instructed to publish and record the same on the New Zealand Companies Register in accordance with s 16 of the Companies Act 1993.

3. APPOINTMENT OF DIRECTORS: RESOLVED that [name of director](s), resident at [address], be and is/are hereby appointed as director(s) of the Company, each holding office from the date of incorporation. The directors are authorized to open bank accounts, appoint a local agent or registered office provider, and execute contracts on behalf of the Company.

4. APPOINTMENT / VACANCY OF COMPANY SECRETARY: RESOLVED that [name], resident at [address], be and is hereby appointed as Company Secretary; in the alternative, RESOLVED that the office of Secretary remains vacant, and the Company will instead rely on its directors for all prescribed administrative duties.

5. CONSOLIDATED GOVERNANCE AND TAX FILINGS: RESOLVED that the directors be and are hereby authorised to apply for the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN), an Inland Revenue Department (IRD) number, Goods and Services Tax (GST) registration (if applicable), to adopt the financial statements preparation policy, to establish a 31 March balance date, and to file all annual returns with the NZCO as required by s 234 of the Companies Act 1993. The directors may further elect any applicable tax exemption or 'International Company' status under the Income Tax Act 2007.

6. DOCUMENTATION: RESOLVED that share certificates be issued, the statutory registers of members, directors, charges, and administrative records be maintained, and the corporate seal (if any) be adopted. This resolution is effective immediately upon incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office online name search module and name reservation facility (companiesoffice.govt.nz / Companies Register electronic name index)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Run an exhaustive exact-match and phonetic/similarity search on the Companies Register using the proposed company name. Ensure the name does not include a restricted word or phrase (e.g., 'Trust', 'Bank', 'Insurance', 'University') without ministerial consent. Reserve the available name via the 'Reserve a Name' online portal, pay the reservation fee, and obtain a unique name reservation number (valid for 20 business days). If no reservation is needed, proceed with incorporation using the final name at the time of filing; the Companies Office will still conduct a final availability check. The name must end with 'LIMITED', 'LTD.', or 'TAPUI' for a Māori-language equivalent.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name in English
Name reservation application form (electronic)
Payment of name reservation fee (NZD 30)
Search result printout demonstrating availability
Written consent of a person if reserved name contains a restricted word
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the requested name is refused or flagged for similarity, promptly select an alternative name and submit a new reservation within the same working day, or submit a written request to the Companies Office seeking written reasons and a reconsideration. If the refusal is based on a similar existing company name, obtain a letter of no objection from the existing company and attach it to a revised incorporation application. In exceptional cases, apply to the High Court for a declaratory judgment under s 13 of the Companies Act 1993 if the refusal is arbitrary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of Constitutional Documents and Director Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Professional formation agent / corporate service provider (acting on behalf of the intending incorporators); National Office of the New Zealand Companies Office will accept the final bundle at filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Company constitution (Form 2) containing the objects clause, share class rights, director powers, quorum rules, and indemnity provisions. Prepare the consent to act as director (Form 3) and shareholder consent to take shares (if not embedded in the constitution). For a company whose directors will be non-resident, appoint one director ordinarily resident in New Zealand (or appoint a New Zealand agent and file the required agent address). Verify that each proposed director is natural person over the age of 20 and is not disqualified under s 151 of the Companies Act 1993. Arrange the registered office / physical service address within New Zealand, typically offered by the corporate agent. Ensure that all statutory forms are signed and dated, and that share subscription amounts are recorded in the ledger.
required_dossiers: Form 2 – Company Constitution (executed copy)
Form 3 – Consent to Appointment of Director(s)
Share subscription and allotment schedule
Consent of Shareholders to take shares
Notice of registered office address (physical New Zealand street address)
Director identification documents (passport / driving licence / utility bill)
Shareholder identity documents for the beneficial owner/registered owner
Declaration of non-disqualification for each director (if not covered by form)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Office requires corrections during pre-lodgement consultation, correct the defective documents within 5 business days and resubmit. Should a director’s consent be invalidated by an irregularity, obtain a fresh signed Form 3 and re-file. If the registered office address is not a physical New Zealand street address, secure a compliant commercial registered office address from a licensed agent and amend the notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Lodgement of Incorporation Application with the New Zealand Companies Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (NZCO) – Company Online electronic filing system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the 'Incorporation' module of the Companies Office online working space. Enter the company name, registered office details, director/shareholder particulars (names, residential addresses, dates of birth, and shareholding percentages), and attach the executed constitution and consent forms. Systematically validate the application by electronic signature of the filing party (usually the director or agent). Submit Form R together with the prescribed government fee of NZD 150 (waived if electronically linked to name reservation). Upon successful online lodgement, the Companies Office will issue an electronic Certificate of Incorporation and automatically generate the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN). The process is typically completed instantly during normal business hours; the statutory maximum processing period is 20 working days. If any field is incomplete, the system will generate a validation alert and prevent submission until corrected.
required_dossiers: Form R – electronic application for incorporation
Filed constitution (Form 2) – incorporated by reference
Form 3 – Director consent(s)
Shareholder consent / share allocation table
Name reservation number and certificate (if reserved)
Electronic payment receipt for NZD 150
Registered office address verification (lease or agent authorization)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a requisition under s 13(2) of the Companies Act 1993 due to non-compliance, the applicant has 20 working days to correct the deficiency, pay any additional required fee, and resubmit the application. If the Registrar rejects the application after requisition, the applicant may request written reasons and, if the rejection is legally erroneous, seek judicial review in the High Court. In practice, most issues are resolved by updating the online form and immediately re-filing during business hours.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) and New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) Register (administered by MBIE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within ten working days of incorporation, ensure that the IRD number is activated by logging into the NZBN / Companies Register which shares data with the IRD. The Company Office issues the NZBN in a single dataset; the IRD number is commonly issued on incorporation but must be confirmed by completing a 'Business Industries and Compliance' questionnaire in myIR. If the company makes taxable supplies exceeding NZD 60,000 per annum, file a GST registration application (IR322). For an 'International Company' tax-exempt classification, submit to the IRD an application under the Foreign Trust/ International Company provisions (e.g., Form IR596 for foreign trust disclosure, or an appropriate declaration under s HR 13 of the Income Tax Act 2007 confirming non-residence and absence of management-control in New Zealand). Also register for PAYE if employees will be engaged, and for RWT on investment income. The directors should elect the first balance date (usually 31 March) and notify the IRD within their first tax return.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (issued electronically)
NZBN certificate (auto-generated)
Company tax information sheet and physical director orders
IR596 / tax status declaration (for international company or foreign trust status)
GST Application Form IR322 (if voluntary or compulsory)
Payroll application (IR334, if employees will be in New Zealand)
Registered office and director details as on the Companies Register
Financial statements forecast for tax estimate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IRD number is not issued automatically, call the IRD Business Helpline or submit an IR742 (Company IRD application). If the IRD queries the International Company designation, provide the Company constitution, bank references, and a written confirmation that management and control are exercised outside New Zealand. If a GST registration is refused because of prospective turnover uncertainty, request voluntary registration under s 51(1)(c) of the GST Act 1985; if late filing penalties arise, apply for penalty remission under s 183A of the Tax Administration Act 1994 with supporting reasonable-cause evidence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Governance Instruments and Compliance Filing Initiation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (annual returns and registry maintenance), WorkSafe New Zealand (health and safety), Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ) and local territorial authorities (physical premises, if any)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first physical or written board meeting to ratify the incorporation, adopt the share certificates, and open corporate bank accounts. Prepare and maintain the statutory registers: register of shareholders, register of directors, register of charges, and record of share allotments. Issue share certificates within 10 working days of allotment. Adopt a minute book and records of all board resolutions for a minimum of 10 years. File the first annual return with the Companies Office within 15 working days after the first anniversary balance date (i.e. typically by 15 April for a 31 March balance date). The annual return confirms the director, shareholder, registered office, and address data are current. If the company will operate an e-sports matchmaking platform without physical premises, obtain a Privacy Act 2020 registration (if holding personal data), and ensure the online terms of use and platform liability policies are drafted. If a physical e-sports centre is established, secure a Building Warrant of Fitness, FENZ fire evacuation scheme approval, and a certificate of public entertainment venue compliance.
required_dossiers: First board meeting minutes or written resolutions file
Share certificate templates and issued share certificates
Register of shareholders and directors (initial filings)
Charges register (nil initial filing, if no security interests)
Annual return filing confirmation (first filing after incorporation)
Privacy Act 2020 register entry (if applicable, for non-NZ data subjects)
Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 compliance statement (even for remote workers)
Optional Industry Code of Practice certificates for e-sports platform operators
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the annual return is filed late, pay the late filing penalty (NZD 200) or apply for remission on the ground of an officer’s serious illness, natural disaster, or invincible accident. If the Companies Office flags a mismatch in director or registered office data, correct the online register immediately by filing a notice of change (Form 5). If WorkSafe or the territorial authority issues an improvement notice, compile a corrective action plan, and apply for reassessment within 10 working days. Any fire safety non-compliance may be remedied by a licensed building surveyor issuing a revised Building Warrant of Fitness certificate.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: New Zealand Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE) – Sectoral Policy and Compliance Unit; for any physical e-sports premises, the territorial authority (city/district council) and Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ) are the responsible permitting bodies. No statutory industrial licence is required for the purely digital ISIC 5820 software publishing and matchmaking platform.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable – no operating licence is statutorily required for an esports tournament matchmaking platform under New Zealand law. Voluntary industry accreditations may include the 'New Zealand Esports Trustmark' and 'Safe Sport Accreditation' for online community moderation. If a physical e-sports arena or event venue is later operated, the relevant permit would be a 'Building Act 2004 Building Warrant of Fitness' and a 'Public Entertainment Event Permit' from the territorial authority.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Not required – an online-only e-sports community platform produces no point-source discharge, waste, or physical industrial activity, and therefore does not require an EIA. If the company later establishes a physical gaming and esports venue, the activity would be classified as a 'Permitted Activity' under the Resource Management (National Environmental Standards for Commercial Hydraulic Activities) Regulations 2021 if all consumptive water use and stormwater thresholds are below 50 m³/day; otherwise a resource consent application would be required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No applicable discharge or emissions standards for the pure digital platform. For any ancillary physical venue, the company must comply with the National Environmental Standards for Air Quality (NZS air contaminants) – specifically, total runoff must not contain waste oil or diesel above 5 mg/L – and the wastewater discharge to municipal sewer must meet the local council’s Trade Waste Bylaw (pH 6.5–10, BOD < 300 mg/L, TSS < 350 mg/L). Non-toxic cooling water and UPS battery banks (if located on any managed server or event site) must comply with the EPA Hazardous Substances Regulations 2017 for contained storage and spill response.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification: If any physical e-sports venue or office is occupied, the building must hold a current Building Warrant of Fitness (BWoF) together with an annual fire evacuation scheme approved by Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ) under the Fire and Emergency New Zealand Act 2017. The evacuation scheme must include a wardening structure and fire training logs. Structural load inspections: A chartered professional engineer must issue a structural load clearance certificate confirming compliance with NZS 1170.5 (earthquake) and AS/NZS 1170.1 (imposed actions), especially for esports spectator seating and server rack installations. Workplace clearance: WorkSafe New Zealand requires the company to provide a safe working environment under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015; for the digital workforce this includes an up-to-date remote-work health and safety policy, incident register, and first-aid arrangements; for any physical event operation, a workplace health and safety audit must be completed before opening to the public.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (New Zealand Inland Revenue / Te Tari Taake); taxpayer portal: myIR via ird.govt.nz; ancillary business registries: New Zealand Companies Office and the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) register.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign (non-resident) entity has no obligation to obtain a New Zealand IRD number unless it derives New Zealand-source income, carries on a taxable activity in New Zealand, or must register for GST. A non-resident company with New Zealand tax obligations applies for an IRD number using Inland Revenue form IR742 (Non-Resident Company Tax Registration), submitted to Inland Revenue by post or through the myIR portal; the same IRD number is used for GST registration (form IR356 or online myIR application). A non-resident supplier of remote/digital services to New Zealand consumers whose supplies exceed NZD 60,000 in a 12-month period must register for GST under the remote services rules using the simplified online registration in myIR. An entity incorporated in New Zealand under the Companies Act 1993 automatically receives an IRD number via the Companies Office issuance of the NZBN and Companies Register number, with the IRD number subsequently confirmed in myIR.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand does not operate a US-style check-the-box election; entity tax status is determined by the Income Tax Act 2007. A New Zealand-resident close company (five or fewer natural person shareholders) may elect Look-Through Company (LTC) status to be treated as a fiscally transparent pass-through entity for all New Zealand tax purposes. There is no standalone hybrid mismatch election; the BEPS hybrid mismatch rules are mandatory statutory provisions (Income Tax Act 2007, subpart FH) that deny deductions or include amounts in income where hybrid entities or financial instruments create mismatch outcomes. For the offshore International Company (CK_IC) in this mandate, the entity is classified as a non-resident company and is taxed on a territorial basis: it is liable to New Zealand income tax only on New Zealand-source income and is outside the New Zealand corporate tax net unless it has a New Zealand permanent establishment or its central management and control is exercised in New Zealand, in which case entity-level taxation at 28% applies, subject to any available LTC election for a qualifying resident close company.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax, legislated and administered in New Zealand as Goods and Services Tax (GST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies in any 12-month period; the same NZD 60,000 annual threshold applies to non-resident suppliers of remote services (including digital and esports platform services) to New Zealand-resident consumers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, no mandatory pre-authorisation of invoices, and no digital fiscal stamping in New Zealand. GST is reported and paid through periodic returns lodged electronically via myIR (typically two-monthly, six-monthly, or quarterly depending on turnover). E-invoicing follows the voluntary Peppol framework; all New Zealand government agencies are required to be able to receive e-invoices, but private businesses have no mandatory e-invoicing obligation. Inland Revenue provides API-based e-services (IR e-services / Gateway) for software-to-Inland Revenue lodgement, but there is no transactional clearance or stamping requirement for individual invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exported goods qualify for 0% GST under section 11 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 when physically exported from New Zealand within the statutory timeframe and evidenced by customs documentation. Exported services qualify under section 11A (services to non-residents) or section 11B (remote services) where the supplier is GST-registered, the recipient is outside New Zealand at the time of supply, and the services are not supplied for consumption in New Zealand. Esports community platform services (tournament matchmaking, subscriptions, digital goods, and platform fees) supplied to non-resident players and communities are zero-rated as remote services where the supplier maintains contemporaneous evidence of the recipient's non-resident status (for example IP address, billing address, or payment method) and payment originates offshore.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (New Zealand Customs Service export entry evidencing physical export, classification, and value)
Bill of Lading (or equivalent Air Waybill / through-shipping document evidencing dispatch from New Zealand)
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank-issued confirmation of foreign currency proceeds received from the offshore purchaser)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue audits zero-rated export claims and may require the full export documentation bundle. Failure to substantiate, or fraudulent claims, trigger reassessment of 15% GST on the supply; late payment penalties (1% per month or part-month under section 142A of the Tax Administration Act 1994); use-of-money interest; and shortfall penalties of 20% (unacceptable tax position), 40% (dominant purpose of tax avoidance), or 150% (abusive or evasive position). Criminal prosecution for evasion or intentional misstatement under section 143A may result in fines up to NZD 250,000 for a company and imprisonment of responsible officers, plus forfeiture and penalties under the Customs and Excise Act 2018 for false export documentation. Retrospective clawback extends across all open assessment periods, generally seven years, and may extend indefinitely where fraud is established.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand operates a fully convertible currency regime without exchange controls under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 1989. Both current account transactions (dividends, royalties, service fees) and capital account transactions (equity injections, loan repayments, acquisition of assets) are freely permitted, with no requirement for central bank approval for profit repatriation or liquidation remittance. The only relevant obstacles are tax compliance obligations (e.g., non-resident withholding tax on dividends and interest, and potential thin capitalisation rules) and standard AML/CFT customer due diligence, neither of which constitutes a currency convertibility barrier.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. New Zealand imposes no statutory obligation to surrender export proceeds, no mandatory conversion timeline, and no minimum conversion ratio for export receipts. Exporters may retain foreign currency in offshore or New Zealand foreign-currency accounts. For balance-of-payments reporting, reserve and monetary statistics reporting obligations attach to registered banks and certain financial institutions, not to the operating export entity.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for payment connectivity, Low for replacement of core banking. Offshore digital EMI providers such as Stripe, PayPal, and Wise Business are viable for collection and disbursement flows of the esports platform, but they cannot serve as the primary regulated deposit-taking institution for corporate treasury. Under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008, any entity providing financial services in or to New Zealand must be registered on the Financial Service Providers Register (FSPR) and hold adequate dispute resolution arrangements. Offshore EMIs are therefore permitted to support payment processing only where they do not constitute unauthorised deposit-taking; capital reserves and statutory escrow balances must be held with a locally licensed New Zealand bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: New Zealand banks generally mandate an in-person or bank-approved video-identity verification for at least one director or an authorised signatory during onboarding. For a non-resident-owned International Company, full remote onboarding is uncommon and is granted only where the entity holds a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN), has a compliant local registered office and physical service address maintained by an approved corporate services provider, and provides enhanced due diligence documentation for the ultimate beneficial owner. For capital escrow and operational account opening, a physical interview is effectively unavoidable for the initial relationship establishment; subsequent signatory changes may be handled remotely.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore or tax-exempt company structure without clear local economic substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of incorporation and certificate of good standing, current register of directors and shareholders, registered agent confirmation, notarised extracts of the corporate register, an organisational chart of the ownership chain, and a written explanation of economic substance and business purpose in New Zealand.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of funds for inbound capital injection or tournament platform revenue
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements or accountant-prepared management accounts, original bank statements for the funding entity, executed capital contribution resolution or shareholder loan agreement, tournament sponsorship contracts, prize pool escrow agreements, and a source-of-wealth declaration supported by tax returns or liquidation proofs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-exempt jurisdiction or Offshore International Company characterisation triggering enhanced due diligence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: An advance tax ruling or legal opinion confirming the tax status, tax residence certificate, evidence of non-residence of strategic management, a demonstration that the structure does not facilitate tax evasion, and, where applicable, a short economic substance report of the offshore entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential exposure to gambling/in-play betting or player-to-player wagering on the esports platform
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A verified legal assessment under the Gambling Act 2003 confirming that the platform is not issuing betting or gambling services, or the applicable licensing exemption; enforceable platform terms of use; strict age-verification procedures; tournament rules; player prize agreements; and a transaction-monitoring policy designed to detect suspicious or criminally-derived funds.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity or quasi-equity injections must be remitted by SWIFT MT103 from the beneficial owner's or subscribing shareholder's account in a reputable jurisdiction. New Zealand does not prescribe a fixed statutory purpose code, but the payment narrative should clearly read 'Capital Contribution' or 'Shareholder Loan' and be accompanied by an internal company resolution, an executed subscription agreement, and a New Zealand Business Number reference where available. The receiving bank will apply enhanced KYCC and may require a FATCA/CRS self-certification (Form W-8BEN-E and CRS FFI form where applicable), as well as evidence of the source of funds. For amounts exceeding NZD 10,000, alack of a clear commercial purpose will trigger an internal suspicious transaction reporting obligation; a compliant capital injection file avoids this outcome.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For international supplier and vendor payments, SWIFT MT103 is the standard clearing rail. For high-value or documentary trade settlements, commercial letters of credit (MT700) and documentary collection (MT400/MT422) are available through New Zealand banks using the messaging and settlement infrastructure underlying the Exchange Settlement Account System (ESAS). For tournament prize payouts and community creator rewards, the platform should use the low-value bulk electronic clearing system for local NZD payments, and SWIFT MT103 or designated EMI rails for cross-border disbursements, with full transaction monitoring and beneficiary verification.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Over-the-counter foreign exchange forward contracts (with a registered New Zealand bank)
Cross-currency swaps for balance-sheet hedging of shareholder loans
FX options (vanilla call and put options)

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) limited to genuine trade-related exposures involving currencies with statutory convertibility restrictions, and only where the underlying commercial risk is demonstrable
Listed foreign exchange futures traded on an approved derivatives exchange where speculative use is not the primary treasury strategy

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Form AR) filed under section 208 of the Companies Act 1993
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office — Companies Register (Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 working days after each anniversary of the company's incorporation date (the annual return date)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs an additional late-filing fee; if overdue, the Registrar may issue a notice of proposed removal and, after 20 working days, deregister (strike off) the company; directors face fines up to NZ$10,000 for non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements and Auditor's Report (where the company is a reporting entity under the Financial Reporting Act 2013)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office — Companies Register (filed electronically, no government fee)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Financial statements must be prepared by the directors within 5 months after the balance date (normally 31 March) and delivered to the Registrar within 20 working days after the date of the auditor's report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to prepare or deliver financial statements and the auditor's report is an offence under the Financial Reporting Act 2013; the company is liable to a fine not exceeding NZ$100,000 and each director to a fine not exceeding NZ$50,000.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Company Income Tax Return (IR4), including any International Questionnaire (IR 320/IR 321) schedules for cross-border transactions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due by 7 July following a standard 31 March balance date; for a non-standard balance date, within 90 days after that balance date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties escalate from NZ$250 to NZ$500 and then NZ$1,000 for repeated overdue returns under the Tax Administration Act 1994; use-of-money interest accrues on unpaid terminal tax; persistent default may lead to prosecution and IRD debt collection action (no administrative strike-off applies under this filing).

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A compulsory independent audit applies where the company is 'large' under the Financial Reporting Act 2013 (consolidated total assets exceeding NZ$10 million or turnover exceeding NZ$50 million), is an FMC reporting entity, or is an overseas-owned company (25% or more non-resident ownership) meeting those thresholds. Small companies are exempt unless required by the constitution, shareholders' resolution, or court order.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand IFRS (NZ IFRS) for large and overseas-owned reporting companies; Reduced Disclosure Regime (NZ IFRS RDR) for non-large reporting entities; simple-format financial statements permitted for small non-reporting companies under the Companies Act 1993.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand does not operate a separate public UBO register; the annual return confirms the directors, shareholders, share structure, and overseas ownership position as at the annual return date. Share transfers must be recorded in the Register of Members and reflected on the next annual return. As an esports platform, the entity is subject to anti-money laundering customer due diligence on beneficial owners under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 180 – 730 per annum (NZ registered office and corporate secretarial agent market; NZD 300 – 1,200)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 – 18,300 per annum (NZD 5,000 – 30,000) for a compulsory audit of a small overseas-owned company; USD 1,200 – 3,000 (NZD 2,000 – 5,000) for a review engagement where no audit is mandated

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays in New Zealand; an offshore International Company with a Tax-Exempt-Zone character and no New Zealand-sourced income bears an effective 0% rate; resident taxpayers may claim a 15% refundable R&D tax credit for eligible R&D expenditure, and no capital gains tax applies to asset disposals.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 (Company Income Tax Return) filed electronically via the Inland Revenue Department's myIR portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 must be filed by 7 July after year-end (without a tax agent); terminal tax is due 7 April; tax-agent extensions defer the filing date to 31 March of the following income year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross turnover - matchmaking fees, tournament entry fees, sponsorship and subscription revenue
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only New Zealand-sourced gross income; foreign-source active income of a non-resident International Company is excluded absent a fixed establishment (PE) in New Zealand.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Rebates, discounts, refunds and allocated prize pool expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only prize payouts made under documented, arm's-length tournament rules and traceable player-payout records that will survive IRD inspection.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total business income after rebates (net income)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile Box 3 to the statutory financial statements of the New Zealand permanent establishment where a NZ PE exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross expenses - platform operations, payment processing fees, player acquisition, server and content costs
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only amounts with sufficient nexus to New Zealand taxable income; excluded are capital items, 50% non-deductible domestic entertainment, and payments subject to NRWT that had no withholding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustments - add-backs of non-deductible expenditure and removal of exempt income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back NRWT-bearing gross-ups, disallowed entertainment expenditure, and any CFC or FIE inclusions; remove exempt offshore dividends.
If a loss results, record the loss for carry-forward; a tax-exempt offshore International Company ordinarily has zero New Zealand taxable income.
A non-resident International Company with a NZ PE computes tax at 28% on PE-attributable profits only; offshore treasury and IP income remain outside the PE scope.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits - imputation credits, foreign tax credits, resident withholding tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits are available only where the IRD holds a certificate of foreign tax paid and the income is within the NZ tax base; attach Form IR907 where applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Residual tax / terminal tax payable or refund
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Terminal tax must be paid through the IRD's electronic banking system from a non-resident bank account; refunds issue to the nominated offshore account after return processing.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: NZ$50 per month or part-month, capped at NZ$250 (Tax Administration Act 1994, s 139A). Late payment penalty: 1% immediately on default plus a monthly incremental penalty of 1% until cleared. Underpaid tax accrues use-of-money interest at the IRD's prescribed rate, updated quarterly. A non-filing entity may be assessed by the Commissioner on default under s 106 TAA 1994, with a 150% shortfall penalty for evasion or an abusive tax position.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) on dividends paid by a New Zealand resident company to a non-resident shareholder; fully imputed dividends qualify for a reduced rate of 15%, and a double taxation agreement (DTA) may lower the rate further (e.g., 5% for a 10% corporate shareholder under the NZ-Australia DTA). In the Tax-Exempt-Zone International Company structure, distributions of offshore profits are not subject to New Zealand dividend NRWT when no New Zealand-source income is involved.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply a DTA rate at source, the non-resident beneficial owner must submit to the payer a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the residence-country tax authority together with a completed IRD Form IR290 (certificate of residence for NRWT purposes); the payer must retain the documentation on file. If a lower rate is denied at source, the recipient claims a refund through the IRD's non-resident withholding tax refund process (Form IR67), attaching the TRC and a declaration of beneficial ownership.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory NRWT 15%, DTA-reduced to 5% (e.g., NZ-Australia) or 10% (e.g., NZ-Canada). Interest: statutory NRWT 15%, commonly 10% under treaties, or replaced by a 2% Approved Issuer Levy (AIL) where the payer is an approved issuer and the interest-bearing security qualifies.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: New Zealand has no statutory Local File/Master File monetary threshold filed with the tax return; the IRD's transfer pricing compliance guidelines require contemporaneous documentation for cross-border related-party transactions in the risk zone of NZ$10 million aggregate goods or NZ$3 million services/royalties/interest, while mandatory Country-by-Country Reporting applies to MNE groups with consolidated revenue of EUR 750 million or more (approximately NZ$1.3 billion).
